findings.headline: Trade-surplus by age is a bell curve peaking at 29, with a cliff after 30 — not the smooth decline the market prices.
findings.stat_summary: Rises $2.7M at age 21 -> peak $8.8M at 29 -> 27-30 window $7.45M vs >30 $4.36M (41% drop) -> $1.77M past 33. WAR mirrors (0.998 at 28 vs 0.298 at 35). Quadratic term p<0.001. Breakpoint gap grows monotonically from $0.46M at cut=28 to $4.5M at cut=33.5. n=3951.
findings.gm_action: Target 27-30; the market's linear aging curve over-credits sub-24 upside and under-marks the post-31 cliff.
findings.novelty: A single linear aging slope averages the rise and the fall, hiding both the 29 peak and the post-30 cliff.

findings.headline: Returns to player quality ACCELERATE at the top — the opposite of diminishing returns.
findings.stat_summary: Surplus slope $60K/unit below quality=0 but $247K/unit above it — 4.1x steeper. Top decile = $16.7M. Convex, quadratic p=0.005. n=2276.
findings.gm_action: Pay up for elite; concentrate prospect capital on the best available rather than spreading across mid-tier targets.
findings.novelty: Markets assume diminishing returns at the top; reality accelerates — elite acquisitions are underpriced per marginal quality unit.

findings.headline: Young-for-level is a threshold, not a slope: the surplus jump is a step at age-relative-to-level > 0.
findings.stat_summary: old-for-level=0.40 surplus-wins, at-level=0.71, young-for-level(>0)=1.64 (2.3x). p=0.001. n=2592.
findings.gm_action: Use young-for-level as a binary screen on prospect returns, not a continuous adjustment.
findings.novelty: The value is a discontinuous step at being young for the level, not a smooth gradient.

dead_ends: FV grade non-linearity: only 0.5% nonzero coverage on acquiring side — 50-FV sweet-spot hypothesis untestable here.
payroll% -> WAR: significant but too jagged to characterize.
contention/pyth thresholds: flat, no switch-on point.
